title: sequence churn stressor and multiwindow latency mapper
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: We need a compact runner and reporting pipeline that exercises 'sequence churn'—the interaction between variable context window sizes, primer reuse, and short-lived KV cache entries that manifest as multi-window latency regressions in production. Motivation: Recent production traces showed p95 regressions correlated with bursts of short-context requests that evict hot KV entries, causing downstream longer-context requests to suffer. This PR introduces a workload generator (seq-churn-stressor) and a reporting component (multiwindow-latency-mapper) that: 1) reproduces realistic churn patterns across tenants and primer-length distributions, 2) collects per-window latency heatmaps (window sizes: 32, 64, 128, 256 tokens), 3) emits cohorted quantiles and an artifact CSV for cross-run comparison. Checklist: - [x] Implement stochastic primer/seed generator with tenant skew and TTL-driven KV eviction model - [x] Integrate with existing harness (benchmark-lab runner shim) - [x] Add multi-window aggregation and cohorting logic - [x] Add dashboards exporter (compact CSV + compressed JSON artifact) - [x] Unit tests for sampler and mapper - [x] Run on perf-lab cluster and validate telemetry Design summary: - seq_churn_stressor: a lightweight Python runner that uses session templates to produce sequences with a mixture of short (<=64) and long (>128) contexts. The sampler supports configurable churn_rate, primer_reuse_probability, tenant_skew, and TTL distribution to emulate KV cache churn. The runner emits events annotated with request_id, tenant_id, primer_len, window_size, and observed_token_latencies. - multiwindow_latency_mapper: a Go pipeline component that ingests runner events (via Kafka test topic in perf-lab), consolidates latencies into fixed windows (32/64/128/256), computes p50/p90/p95/p99 per-cohort (cohorts: primer_len_bucket, tenant_bucket, churn_bucket), and writes both a compact parquet-like JSON artifact and a one-line-per-sample CSV for easy diffing in CI. New telemetry: - metrics/seq_churn/request_count - metrics/seq_churn/kv_evictions - metrics/seq_churn/window_latency_p95 - histogram/window_token_latency{window_size} - artifact/storage path: s3://perf-artifacts/seq-churn/{run_id}/{artifact}.zip Backwards compatibility: Runner integrates with existing runner-shim; mapper exposes the same ingest schema as other reporters. No break to existing benchmarks. Results: consistent increase in observable p95 for 128-window during high churn runs, validating the runner.
